issues.note: Right: fabric can also be knitted or felted; the definition is too narrow.
'Tall fabric' is not a natural collocation; fabric is not tall.
The factory confusion is stated in four fields, against the one-fact-one-field rule.
Entry-level adaptation repeats the factory point made in other fields.
Usage note sentence restates the learner-error and adaptation factory point.
Naming Spanish and Portuguese breaks the language-neutral rule for adaptation notes.
The plural is marginal; 'the fabric of' is essentially singular, so the label is fine.

findings.F1: Sense 1 definition limits fabric to woven material, excluding knitted and felted cloth.
findings.F3: Sense 1 false-friends adaptation note names specific languages.
findings.F4: The fabric/factory confusion is repeated across the sense adaptation, entry adaptation, usage note, and learner error.

missed: Sense 1 definition uses hard defining words (interlacing, filaments, warp and weft) that a B1 learner cannot read; no issue objected on that ground.
